name: California
status_why: The Secretary's public JSON service answered scripts and already carries the Nov 3 contests, with test numbers.
system: California Secretary of State's own election-night reporting: electionresults.sos.ca.gov (nginx behind CloudFront and Imperva) with a public JSON service at api.sos.ca.gov/returns/

results_page.label: California Secretary of State: election results

election.how_to_find: The service serves the current election; nothing to find.

feeds.address: https://api.sos.ca.gov/returns/<office> (governor answered: raceTitle, Reporting, ReportingTime, candidates[Name, Party, Votes, Percent, incumbent]); https://api.sos.ca.gov/returns/status (59 entries: each county's precincts reporting, turnout, registered, report timestamps, countyLink, plus 'statewide')
feeds.updates: counties report to the Secretary through the night (the Elections Code asks at least every two hours on election night; check the section before quoting it); the ReportingTime field changes with each update
feeds.note: 2026-10-09: /returns/governor and /returns/status answered 200 to the script (X-CDN Imperva, no challenge). The feed is already loaded with the Nov 3, 2026 contests and TEST numbers (e.g. governor 'October 9, 2026, 2:53 p.m.', 20.2% reporting), while /returns/status still carries September 2024 test timestamps. Never show anything before 8 p.m. Pacific on Nov 3; treat any value before then as test data.
No Senate race in California in 2026. Top-two general: both candidates may share a party.

feeds.updates: LA posts on election night, then on a published schedule until certification
feeds.note: results.lavote.gov answered 200 (12 KB shell, Imperva script embedded); its data calls were not traced. Each county's results link is in /returns/status (countyLink).

races_in_feed: the Secretary's feed: statewide offices, Congress, legislature, ballot measures (judges: Supreme Court and appellate retention likely; superior court judges are county). County, city, school and special-district contests only on the 58 counties' own sites.
local: Yes, 58. Los Angeles (results.lavote.gov), San Diego (sdvote.gov), Orange (ocvote.gov), Riverside and Santa Clara (both refused scripts with Cloudflare 403 in the 2026-09-30 scouting), San Bernardino, San Francisco (sfelections.org, ranked-choice).
how_counted: Counties report through the night and keep counting for weeks; the Secretary of State certifies 38 days after the election.
count_order: No ballot-type split in the feed; the Secretary's Unprocessed Ballots Report (mail against provisional, by county) is the count-order input.
vote_types: No: the Secretary's feed gives totals and precincts reporting only. The Secretary's Unprocessed Ballots Report (by county, mail vs provisional) is the count-order input; counties' own sites sometimes split vote-by-mail and in-person.

rules.note: The two who advanced from the June primary; both may share a party.

certify.rule: On the 38th day after the election, or sooner if every return is in (Cal. Elec. Code 15503, 15504).
certify.local_rule: Counties certify within 30 days (Cal. Elec. Code 15372).
certify.source: NCSL, 'Election Certification Deadlines' (www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/certification-deadlines), read 2026-10-10; secondary: a summary of each state's law, not the law itself

rehearsal: the service's current figures (its test numbers for the November 3 contests); it serves no past election
terms: none seen on the API responses
scout_blocked: nothing on the Secretary's feed; Riverside and Santa Clara county sites refuse scripts (Cloudflare 403, per local_scout.json)
scout_plan: Poll api.sos.ca.gov/returns/governor, the other statewide offices and /returns/us-rep/district/all every few minutes from 8 p.m. Pacific, keyed on ReportingTime, with /returns/status for county reporting; rehearse against the test numbers it serves now. Because California counts for weeks, keep updating daily until certification and label the reporting share. Local results: one reader per county, Los Angeles first (results.lavote.gov), then San Diego, Orange and San Bernardino, which answered scripts in September.
notes: The feed serves TEST numbers today (2026-10-09). Nothing before 8 p.m. Pacific on Nov 3 is real.
Paths confirmed 2026-10-10: returns/<office>/county/all for the eight statewide offices; returns/us-rep, state-senate, state-assembly and board-of-equalization /district/all (districtwide only).
The Supreme Court and Court of Appeal retention votes are not read (no address for them found on the service); the pages link to the Secretary's own results for them.
sources: NCSL, 'Election Certification Deadlines' (www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/certification-deadlines), read 2026-10-10; secondary: a summary of each state's law, not the law itself
